passage_text: Isogenic E. coli strains carrying single repair defects were grown for many generations, and the spontaneous mutation rate was measured by fluctuation analysis at a neutral locus. UV survival was measured after a fixed dose of 254 nm light. Table 1 reports the spontaneous rate per 10 to the ninth base pairs per generation and the percentage of cells surviving the UV dose. Wild-type cells repair mismatches, bulky lesions, oxidized bases and double-strand breaks.
table_data:
| Strain | Spontaneous rate | UV survival (%) |
|---|---|---|
| Wild type | 0.002 | 100 |
| mutS minus | 0.15 | 96 |
| uvrA minus | 0.004 | 12 |
| recA minus | 0.30 | 0.5 |
| polA exonuclease minus | 0.12 | 55 |
| photolyase minus | 0.003 | 40 |
stem: Which strain has a defect in mismatch repair?
explanation: mutS encodes a protein that recognizes mismatched base pairs formed during replication, so losing it raises the spontaneous mutation rate 75-fold while leaving UV survival nearly intact. The mismatch repair pathway does not remove UV photoproducts, which is why the UV phenotype is mild. uvrA, recA and photolyase defects instead affect damage repair after UV exposure.
memorize: mutS and mutL recognize replication mismatches; mutH nicks the new strand

fm.formula: fold increase = mutant rate / wild-type rate
fm.variables: Rates are per base pair per generation
fm.why: Mismatch repair corrects errors that escape proofreading, so its loss multiplies the residual error rate
fm.no_calc: Two orders of magnitude above the wild type means a repair defect

correct_rationale_plain: The mutS mutant has a large spontaneous mutation rate with near-normal UV survival, the signature of defective mismatch repair.

wrong.A: uvrA is needed for nucleotide excision repair of bulky lesions and shows strong UV sensitivity
wrong.C: recA is required for recombination repair and is extremely UV sensitive
wrong.D: Photolyase repairs pyrimidine dimers using visible light

sc: High spontaneous rate plus normal UV equals mismatch repair.

stem: The uvrA mutant shows a normal spontaneous mutation rate but only 12 percent UV survival. What does uvrA encode?

options.B: A photolyase that uses visible light
options.C: A component of nucleotide excision repair that removes bulky lesions such as thymine dimers
options.D: The proofreading exonuclease of DNA polymerase

explanation: Nucleotide excision repair recognizes helix-distorting lesions, nicks the damaged strand on both sides and removes a short oligonucleotide. UV light creates thymine dimers, which are substrates for this pathway, so losing uvrA causes marked UV sensitivity. uvrA, uvrB and uvrC are the bacterial NER nuclease components

fm.formula: repair pathway choice depends on lesion structure
fm.variables: NER handles bulky adducts; mismatch repair handles replication errors; base excision repair handles small oxidized bases

fm.why: Thymine dimers distort the helix enough to recruit the NER machinery, which excises a patch around the damage
fm.no_calc: Normal spontaneous rate plus UV sensitivity equals NER defect

wrong.B: Photolyase is a separate light-dependent enzyme, and its mutant has 40 percent survival
wrong.D: Proofreading is the polA exonuclease, whose mutant also has a high spontaneous rate

sc: UV sensitive with normal spontaneous rate equals NER.
mn: uvrA cuts out the UV blister.

stem: Why is the recA mutant the most UV-sensitive strain in Table 1?

options.C: recA encodes a base excision repair glycosylase

stem: The polA exonuclease mutant has a 60-fold higher spontaneous mutation rate. What function did it lose?

options.C: The helicase activity that unwinds the duplex
options.D: The ligase activity that seals nicks

wrong.C: Helicase activity is encoded by separate genes such as dnaB

stem: What reaction does photolyase catalyze after UV exposure?

options.A: It removes oxidized guanine from DNA
options.B: It uses visible light to split pyrimidine dimers back into separate bases

stem: How does mismatch repair know which strand to correct?

options.A: It removes both strands and resynthesizes the entire region
options.B: It always corrects the older strand because it is more accurate
options.C: It uses transient hemimethylation of the parental strand to identify the newly synthesized strand
options.D: It relies on the sequence of the mismatch to decide which base is wrong

explanation: In E. coli, adenine methylation at GATC sites lags behind replication, so the newly made strand is transiently unmethylated. fm.no_calc: Methylation marks the old strand as correct

wrong.A: Repair is local and strand-specific, not a wholesale replacement
wrong.B: The older strand is protected by methylation rather than by being more accurate
wrong.D: The mismatch itself does not reveal which base is wrong; strand age does

stem: A single base insertion occurs in the middle of a coding exon. What is the most likely consequence?

options.A: A frameshift that changes every downstream codon and usually truncates the protein
options.B: A silent mutation with no change in the protein
options.C: A single amino acid substitution only
options.D: No effect because the genetic code is degenerate

explanation: Codons are read in nonoverlapping triplets, so inserting one base shifts the reading frame from that point onward. All downstream codons change, and a premature stop codon usually appears, truncating the protein. Degeneracy protects against some substitutions but cannot absorb an insertion that is not a multiple of three.

wrong.C: A single substitution changes one amino acid; an insertion changes the frame
wrong.D: Degeneracy applies to third-base substitutions, not to insertions

sc: One base in or out equals frameshift.
mn: Off by one, ruined to the end.

stem: Which pathway removes 8-oxoguanine and deaminated cytosine from DNA?
explanation: Base excision repair starts with a glycosylase that cleaves the base from the sugar, leaving an abasic site that is then processed and filled by a short patch of DNA synthesis. It handles small, non-helix-distorting lesions such as oxidized bases and uracil from cytosine deamination. NER handles bulky lesions, and mismatch repair handles replication errors.
memorize: Base excision repair removes small modified bases via glycosylases
Uracil-DNA glycosylase removes uracil from deaminated cytosine

fm.formula: glycosylase cleaves the N-glycosidic bond, creating an abasic site
fm.variables: The lesion is a single modified base that does not distort the helix
fm.values: not needed; lesion size determines the pathway
fm.why: A single damaged base is removed individually, leaving the backbone to be repaired by a short patch
fm.no_calc: Small lesion equals base excision repair

correct_rationale_plain: Base excision repair removes oxidized or deaminated bases one at a time, starting with a glycosylase.

wrong.B: NER removes bulky, helix-distorting lesions such as UV dimers
wrong.C: Mismatch repair corrects replication errors, not oxidized bases

passage_text: Isogenic E. coli strains carrying single repair defects were grown for many generations, and the spontaneous mutation rate was measured by fluctuation analysis at a neutral locus. UV survival was measured after a fixed dose of 254 nm light. Table 1 reports the spontaneous rate per 10 to the ninth base pairs per generation and the percentage of cells surviving the UV dose. Wild-type cells repair mismatches, bulky lesions, oxidized bases and double-strand breaks.
table_data:
| Strain | Spontaneous rate | UV survival (%) |
|---|---|---|
| Wild type | 0.002 | 100 |
| mutS minus | 0.15 | 96 |
| uvrA minus | 0.004 | 12 |
| recA minus | 0.30 | 0.5 |
| polA exonuclease minus | 0.12 | 55 |
| photolyase minus | 0.003 | 40 |
stem: Xeroderma pigmentosum causes extreme skin cancer risk after sun exposure. Which defect underlies it?

options.B: Loss of base excision repair glycosylases

explanation: Xeroderma pigmentosum is caused by mutations in nucleotide excision repair genes, so UV-induced pyrimidine dimers persist and cause mutations in skin cells. Patients must avoid sunlight because every exposure adds unrepaired damage. The disorder is distinct from mismatch repair defects, which cause hereditary nonpolyposis colon cancer.
memorize: Xeroderma pigmentosum equals defective nucleotide excision repair
Lynch syndrome equals defective mismatch repair

fm.formula: unrepaired UV dimers become mutations at the next replication
fm.variables: NER removes the dimer before replication; without it, translesion synthesis introduces mutations
fm.values: not needed; the pathway identifies the disease
fm.why: Persistent dimers block replication and are bypassed by error-prone polymerases, producing mutations
fm.no_calc: Sun sensitivity plus skin cancer equals NER defect

correct_rationale_plain: Xeroderma pigmentosum results from defective nucleotide excision repair, so UV dimers persist and cause mutations.

wrong.A: Mismatch repair defects cause hereditary colon cancer, not photosensitivity
wrong.B: Base excision repair defects do not produce the classic UV sensitivity of this disorder
wrong.D: Telomerase defects cause bone marrow failure and pulmonary fibrosis

stem: Why does the uvrA mutant keep a nearly normal spontaneous mutation rate while the mutS mutant does not?

options.A: uvrA only repairs damage caused by chemicals, not by replication
options.B: uvrA is not expressed unless cells are irradiated
options.C: Spontaneous mutations do not occur in E. coli
options.D: Nucleotide excision repair targets externally induced bulky lesions, while mismatch repair corrects the replication errors that dominate the spontaneous rate

explanation: Spontaneous mutations arise mainly from replication errors and from endogenous base damage that base excision repair handles. Nucleotide excision repair is dedicated to bulky, helix-distorting lesions such as UV dimers, which are rare without an external insult, so losing it barely changes the spontaneous rate. The UV survival column shows the phenotype that uvrA loss does produce.
memorize: Each repair pathway has a distinct lesion specificity
Spontaneous mutations come mainly from replication errors

fm.formula: spontaneous rate reflects replication fidelity plus endogenous damage repair
fm.variables: NER handles bulky adducts; mismatch repair handles replication errors
fm.why: A pathway only affects the mutation rate to the extent that its substrate lesions occur under the growth conditions
fm.no_calc: Twofold versus 75-fold tells you which pathway handles spontaneous errors

correct_rationale_plain: NER's substrates are rare without UV exposure, while mismatch repair handles the replication errors that drive the spontaneous rate.

wrong.A: NER repairs UV and chemical adducts, and it is not the main spontaneous-error pathway
wrong.B: uvrA is expressed constitutively as part of the SOS regulon and is not irradiation-gated
wrong.C: Spontaneous mutations certainly occur; that is what the assay measures

sc: Lesion specificity explains which mutant changes which rate.
mn: NER waits for sunlight; mismatch repair works every division.
